service_account.token.rotate.issuedCredential: Requires explicit future UTC expiresAt within operator limits and an eligible stored token/service credential; delegated OAuth cannot execute these token-only actions. Only the new downstream credential appears in result.issuedToken, alongside accessToken metadata. Broker execution credentials remain private. Sensitivity markers are advisory: use private delivery; later use follows GitLab permissions, not Broker grants.
service_account.token.rotate.rotation: Preserves the active token's identity/permissions after checking current limits; expiry must be explicit. Revoked/inactive tokens are not rotated. previousTokenId always identifies the old token, while tokenId is present only for a different returned new ID. Inspect/revoke/reconcile an uncertain rotation rather than rotating again.
service_account.token.rotate.recovery: An uncertain response uses applied_unverified at mutation_response with only safe numeric IDs. Metadata reads cannot recover the secret. Inspect the account/token list and revoke or reconcile a possibly issued credential before retrying; no automatic rollback or replay occurs.
service_account.token.rotate.ownership: The project service-account endpoint must prove userId belongs to this project. An ordinary user or another project's account cannot be substituted.
service_account.token.rotate.membership: Requires existing direct membership within the configured role cap; it does not change membership. Higher-role accounts may still have tokens revoked through the separately granted revoke action.
